measurer_summary.question: A2: join completeness. Per corpus, per SWE-chat format, and split by is_subagent: orphan results, calls without a result, duplicate call_ids within a session, calls with more than one result. Rates are session-clustered, run on the Phase A split only. Also: how much the raw transcripts recover compared with conversations.parquet (cited numbers).

surprises: Most of SWE-chat's Gemini gap is one session. A single session uses a bare {messages:[...]} export variant with 487 calls and no results at all. Its 486 distinct unpaired keys equal the full-population Gemini calls_without_result count (486), so this one session plausibly accounts for the format's census share of 0.0926. That attribution is not verified.

The SWE-chat release redacted some Gemini call ids to the literal string 'REDACTED', and the Gemini loader kept them. For OpenCode the loader replaced such ids with synthetic ones. This produces the only duplicate call key found. It is harmless here only because that session has no results.

In honest Claude Code sessions, missing results are rare per call but common per session. 20/127 swechat CC sessions = 0.157 [0.104, 0.231] have at least one call with no result. They cluster at compaction boundaries (7) and SessionStart restart/resume hooks (6), not only at session end (13).
In 4 of 7 unpaired Task/Agent calls, the subagent visibly ran (nested events exist) but the parent never got a tool_result.
In aiv_cu, 0.5556 [0.5020, 0.6102] of result events carry no output text. A result being present does not mean its content is present.

Call ids are not unique across sessions. swechat has 204 shared ids (198 are loader synthetic ids, which are per-format-seq), aiv_cu has 50 provider ids repeated across 4 sessions, and whowhen step ids repeat by construction.

1,804 swechat main-stream meta events have a parent_call_id that does not resolve to any call. Nearly all are Stop (1,189) and SessionStart (613) hook_progress events whose parent id is not a tool call. Every tool-attached timer type does resolve (bash_progress 6,033/6,033).
implications_for_phase_b: Build every pair-conditioned mechanism on the raw-transcript IR, never on conversations.parquet. The table orphans 0.1877 of results and has no Codex or Cursor calls; raw has 16 results without a call in 633,366.

Exclude by rule, not by format label: sessions with calls but zero results (swechat Cursor, plus the Gemini bare-export session); Codex server_side_tool calls; and Who&When AG calls with extra.unexecuted. Treat these as 'no evidence', not as 'missing result'.

A 'call with no result' signal has an honest baseline of about 16% of swechat Claude Code sessions [0.104, 0.231], but only 1/107 cc_local sessions and 4/78 aiv_cc runs. Any detector built on unanswered calls must first condition on stream end, compact_boundary and SessionStart landmarks; otherwise its false-positive floor will vary by corpus.

aiv_cu cannot test join completeness, because pairing is by construction. Mechanisms that compare a claim with a tool output must condition on output being non-empty (only 0.4444 of results have text). Unexecuted provider calls (extra.unexecuted_calls) are a separate channel.

Who&When AG code blocks that were never executed (12/99 calls in A; 43/279 in the population, cited) are a natural place to probe 'claims a result for code that never ran'. Pairing there is assigned by the loader, so any HC result must be treated as heuristic.
Always join on (session_id, call_id). Synthetic, provider and step ids collide across sessions.

Latency and progress mechanisms (A1) can rely on parent_call_id links. Tool-attached progress and end records resolve 100% in A, apart from one Codex web_search_end and one PostToolUse hook. Filter out Stop and SessionStart hooks, which are not tool-linked.

Parent attribution for session-level subagents (Codex, OpenCode) cannot be done inside the Phase A split. Codex: 0 of 5 parent ids resolve in A. OpenCode: 3 of 9 resolve. 9 of 23 subagent sessions have no parent id. Any parent-child mechanism needs the population, not one split.
could_not_measure: Whether all 486 population Gemini calls without a result come from the one Phase A session. The counts are equal, but confirming it would mean opening B caches or raw files beyond one exploratory check, so it was not done.
Source-side join completeness for aiv_cu. The loader emits a result per executed call from the same row, so an orphan or unpaired call cannot appear in the IR.
Whether the Who&When HC open-call pairing heuristic and the AG adjacency pairing are correct. No ground truth exists for the pairings themselves.
The cause of the one Claude Code orphan classed 'other', and of the 4 'other' unpaired CC calls. Classification used only IR fields, with no text inspection.

Table-vs-raw rates restricted to Phase A sessions. The task said to cite rather than recompute, and the cited cross-check covers the combined A+B sample (2,200 sessions) while the recon covers the whole table, so no A-only table comparison exists.
Bootstrap CIs for zero counts are degenerate ([0, 0]). For those cases the only informative bound is the Wilson interval on sessions affected (for example aiv_cu 0/199, upper bound 0.019).

One correction to the hedging: the census counts calls_without_result as distinct keys (load_swechat.py line 1135 iterates over cset; 5246 - 4759 = 487 ≠ 486 confirms it). The session has 486 distinct unpaired keys and is itself part of the census, so the other 58 Gemini files contribute exactly 0. The 'plausible, not verified' attribution is arithmetically entailed. The census numerator (distinct keys) and denominator (call events) use mixed units, which is negligible here.

A bootstrap over 2 clusters has only 3 possible outcomes, and its upper bound of 0.0082 is just the affected session's own rate. The 'usable' verdict depends on that degenerate bound. Under per-call Wilson the upper bound is 0.021 > 0.01, which would give 'partial'. The honest label is 'insufficient n'.

checks.my_numbers: Checked against the sources. recon/swechat_scan_pinned.json: orphaned 76618 of 408086 distinct results, hidden subagent tool_use 172814. recon/swechat_compare.txt: 1367/1367 orphan ids found as top-level tool_use in raw. phase_c swechat_tables.json followup pooled_dropped_share: 76258/407920 = 0.1869 [0.1804, 0.1927], n=4847. build full_population_pass: results without call 16/633366, calls without result 2104/635454, nested 176501. build crosscheck_conversations: 171329 raw vs 133018 table in 2159 present sessions; 1671 sessions where raw has more; codex 96 and cursor 15 sessions with 0 table rows; 162 table ids not in raw, all opencode.
checks.problem: The 162 ids are misattributed. They come from one salvaged OpenCode session where the raw parse is truncated, not from REDACTED-id handling (see the opencode check). The 1367/1367 orphan-id check covers 48 sessions, not 50: 2 of the 50 sampled sessions had no transcript file. The headline contrast 0.1877 vs 0.0000253 compares different units (table-wide distinct ids vs result events) over different session sets (5825 vs 5850). The order-of-magnitude gap holds, but the comparison is not matched.

overclaims: The '162 table ids missing from raw, all OpenCode REDACTED-id handling' attribution is wrong. All 162 come from one salvaged, truncated OpenCode document, ses_3353a8139ffeLXvY9MIuOitgt6, which is in split A: 185 raw IR calls vs 417 table tool_use rows. For that session the table recovers more than the raw IR, and A2's join metrics cannot detect the loss.

The swechat/copilot 'usable' verdict rests on a 2-cluster bootstrap upper bound of 0.0082, which is the affected session's own rate. Per-call Wilson for 1/266 has an upper bound of 0.0210, above the 0.01 threshold. The verdict should be 'insufficient n'.

Zero-count 'usable' verdicts (opencode, aiv_cu, and every zero orphan, duplicate or multi-result rate) pass only because the bootstrap gives [0, 0] when there are no defects. The rule's 'hi' does not bound those rates: the OpenCode census rate 0.0003 lies outside A's [0, 0], and session-level Wilson upper bounds reach 0.133 for opencode. The measurer computed those Wilson bounds but did not use them in the verdict.

The 0.01 verdict threshold was set after the swechat-A unpaired counts had been seen, against the instruction to set thresholds first. The measurer disclosed this. Verdicts that sit close to the threshold (copilot 0.0082) are the ones it affects.
Calling aiv_cu 'usable' overstates it: its 0/6107 is a product of how the loader builds rows, so the data cannot test it.

The corpus-wide claim 'no result comes before its call' holds by construction for aiv_cu, opencode, gemini and whowhen, where the loader emits the result right after its call. It is an observation only for claude_code, codex, cc_local and aiv_cc.

The 1-call sessions and runs classed as structural (session_has_no_results) include a swechat claude_code stream end and an aiv_cc run that ended in error_during_execution. Both are lost results, not format gaps. Verdicts do not change.

'They cluster at compaction boundaries (7) and SessionStart restart/resume hooks (6)' is not established. The reasons come from a first-match rule that checks whether a landmark falls inside the window between the call and the stream's next result, which can span hundreds or thousands of events. There is no baseline rate, and the counts are small (SessionStart is 6 calls in 3 sessions).
'In honest Claude Code sessions': SWE-chat carries no honesty label. 'Honest' is an assumption about the baseline, not something measured.
'All 1,367 orphan ids from 50 of the 4,386 orphan-bearing sessions': 2 of the 50 sampled sessions had no transcript file, so the ids come from 48.
The summary's '694 are structural' should be 695 (206 + 488 + 1). The JSON is correct.
